## Basic_objects

- [what are booleans? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/booleans/booleans.html): What are booleans in Python? TDD chapter (project booleans, uv init, pytest-watcher) that divides basic objects into False and True groups with unittest. Builds test_what_is_false / test_what_is_true (bool and int instances; not float/str/tuple/list/set/dict; assertIs identity; bool() then assertFalse/assertTrue). Then falsy/truthy drills for None, integers, floats, strings, tuples, lists, sets, dictionaries — each with bool(x), bare assertFalse/assertTrue, and assertIsNot vs False/True so 0, 0.0, '', empty containers, and None are falsy but not the False object. Ends with numeric values: False is 0 (ZeroDivisionError on 1/False), True is 1. Introduces assertFalse / assertTrue raise-by-negation. Real errors: AssertionError False != True, True is not false, 0 is not False, 0.0 is not False. Next: truth table. Part of Jacob Itegboje's Pumping Python series.
- [test booleans with loops | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/booleans/booleans_w_loops.html): Beginner Python TDD tutorial — test booleans with loops. Continues the booleans project (pytest-watcher, git) and uses for loops plus subTest to remove repeated unittest checks. Extracts test_what_are_booleans over (False, True) with assertIsInstance of (bool, int), assertNotIsInstance of float/tuple/str/list/set/dict, and assertIs identity. Loops assert_is_not_the_same_as_false_or_true over False and True (assertNotEqual and assertIsNot; 28 subtests). Extracts test_what_is_falsy for None, '', (), [], set(), and {} (assertFalse on bool(x) and on x) and test_what_is_truthy for -1, -0.1, 0.1, a non-empty string, tuple, list, set, and dict. Then test_the_value_of_false loops 0 and 0.0: equal to False, not the False object, not equal to True, not the True object, and falsy. Real AssertionError strings: "None is not an instance of any of (<class 'bool'>, <class 'int'>)", "False is not true", "None is not true", "True is not false", "-1 is not false", "0 != True", "0 == False", "0 is not true". Part of Jacob Itegboje's Pumping Python series.
- [booleans | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/booleans/index.html)
- [what is a dictionary? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/dictionaries.html): Python dictionaries TDD tutorial by Jacob Itegboje (Pumping Python): create dicts with dict() and {}, test which basic objects work as hashable keys (None, booleans, ints, floats, tuples) vs unhashable keys raising TypeError (list, set, dict), inspect dir(dict) with self.maxDiff = None, and test all 11 dict methods (clear, copy, fromkeys, get, items, keys, pop, popitem, setdefault, update, values), dict_items/dict_keys/dict_values NameError -> list(), dict comprehensions, and KeyError in unittest.
- [basic objects | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/index.html): Python basic objects for beginners: the complete beginner-friendly guide to None (the simplest), Booleans (True/False and truthiness), Lists, and Dictionaries. Learn by testing with TDD, assertions, is vs ==, and real examples that distinguish identity from value (e.g. why 0 == 0.0 but 0 is not 0.0, why empty things are falsy but not the same object as False or None). Builds on the AssertionError chapters with setUp refactoring, unittest testing patterns, and red-green-refactor for each structure. Covers what None really is, boolean operators and truthiness gotchas, list and dict basics through practical tests.
- [what is a list? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/lists/index.html): Python lists for beginners: step-by-step TDD tutorial testing mutable sequence objects with unittest and pytest. Learn how to create lists with list() and [], explore dir(list) and dir(object) with maxDiff = None, and test all list methods: append, clear, copy, count, extend, index, insert, pop, remove, reverse, and sort. Master 0-based indexing, negative indexing, item assignment (mutation), slicing ([start:stop]), and the exceptions every beginner encounters: TypeError ('int' object is not iterable), ValueError ('not in list' is not in list), and IndexError (list index out of range, pop from empty list).
- [what is a list comprehension? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/lists/list_comprehensions.html): Beginner Python TDD tutorial for list comprehensions by Jacob Itegboje (Pumping Python). Learn to create, filter, and transform lists with [x for x in ...] syntax, if conditions, and functions through red-green-refactor with unittest. TestCase.setUp resets instance attributes (self.a_list, self.an_iterable) to prevent shared mutation state. Compares list comprehensions with for loops, list(), extend(), filter(), map(), itertools.filterfalse, and lambdas. Real Python errors: AssertionError "True is not false", "Lists differ: [0, 1, 2, ...] != []", TypeError "takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given", "list.extend() takes exactly one argument", AttributeError "has no attribute 'a_list'", and TypeError "'bool' object is not callable".
- [none | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/none/index.html)
- [what is None? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/none/none.html): Beginner Python TDD tutorial — what is None? (the simplest object / singleton). Project ``none``: uv init, pytest-watcher, git. test_what_is_none keeps assertIs(None, None) beside assertIsNone(None); then red-green-refactor "is None a boolean / int / float / str / tuple / list / set / dict?" with assertIsNotNone, assertIsInstance, assertNotIsInstance. Shows None is not False, 0, 0.0, '', (), [], set(), or {}. Real AssertionError strings: "unexpectedly identical: None", "unexpectedly None", "False is not None", "0 is not None", "{} is not None", "None is not an instance of <class 'bool'>". Introduces assertIsNone / assertIsNotNone (parallel to assert x is None / is not None); reuses assertIsInstance / assertNotIsInstance; digression that {} is empty dict while set() is empty set. Builds on AssertionError (assertIs / assertIsNot) before booleans/truthiness. Part of Jacob Itegboje's Pumping Python series.
- [test None with loops | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/basic_objects/none/none_w_loops.html): Beginner Python TDD tutorial — what is None? (the simplest object / singleton). Project ``none``: uv init, pytest-watcher, git. test_what_is_none keeps assertIs(None, None) beside assertIsNone(None); then red-green-refactor "is None a boolean / int / float / str / tuple / list / set / dict?" with assertIsNotNone, assertIsInstance, assertNotIsInstance. Shows None is not False, 0, 0.0, '', (), [], set(), or {}. Real AssertionError strings: "unexpectedly identical: None", "unexpectedly None", "False is not None", "0 is not None", "{} is not None", "None is not an instance of <class 'bool'>". Introduces assertIsNone / assertIsNotNone (parallel to assert x is None / is not None); reuses assertIsInstance / assertNotIsInstance; digression that {} is empty dict while set() is empty set. Builds on AssertionError (assertIs / assertIsNot) before booleans/truthiness. Part of Jacob Itegboje's Pumping Python series.

## Exceptions

- [what is an assertion? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AssertionError/AssertionError.html): Step-by-step beginner Python TDD tutorial that teaches AssertionError by deliberately triggering it with bare `assert`. See exactly why a bare comparison like `1 + 1 == 11` (or reality == my expectation) does not fail the test or raise an error—Python just evaluates it and continues—while `assert` turns a false result into AssertionError and stops. Understand the pytest output beginners actually see on bare asserts ("E   assert False is True", "E       assert 0 != 0.0", collection ERROR vs FAILED, and "no tests ran" when there are no `test_*` functions yet). Master `=` (assignment) vs `==` (equality) and especially `is` / `is not` (identity, same object) vs `==` / `!=` (value equality). Concrete examples with None, True, False, 0 vs 0.0 (0 == 0.0 is True but 0 is not 0.0), strings, lists, dicts, sets, tuples using only bare `assert`. Learn to group assertions in functions so pytest names the tests and gives clear failure messages instead of "no tests ran". Full project setup with `uv init`, `tests/__init__.py` package, `uv add --requirement requirements.txt` (pytest + pytest-watcher), `uv run pytest-watcher . --now --patterns "**/*.py"`, `git add` + `git commit --all --message` after every change, and the complete red-green-refactor cycle (including "remove the commented lines" and turning top-level asserts into `def test_*`). Perfect for absolute beginners learning Python testing, why bare expressions are ignored, pytest collection rules, None/True/False/0 identity gotchas, and how assertions control test outcomes.
- [test AssertionError with functions | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AssertionError/AssertionError_w_functions.html): Pumping Python TDD continuation: "test AssertionError with functions" in the assertion_error project. Reuse `assert_equal(x, y)` from extract assert_equal, then extract `assert_not_equal`, `assert_is_not`, `assert_is_not_none`, `assert_is_not_false`, and `assert_is_not_true` so repeated bare asserts become helper calls. Walk red-green-refactor on test_assert_keyword, test_assertion_error_w_equality, test_assertion_error_w_is_vs_equal (0 is not 0.0 but 0 == 0.0), test_assertion_error_w_none/false/true, and test_failure. See pytest cores like `assert 2 == 3`, `assert '11' == '2'`, `assert None != None`, `assert None is not None`, `assert False is not False`. uv run pytest-watcher . --now --patterns "**/*.py", git commit after each extract. Helpers sit above the tests; pytest still only runs test_* names (will_not_run skipped).
- [test AssertionError with generators | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AssertionError/AssertionError_w_generators.html): Beginner Python TDD tutorial (Jacob Itegboje, Pumping Python): test AssertionError with generators in the assertion_error project. Open existing project with uv run pytest-watcher . --now --patterns "**/*.py". Replace nested for loops across basic_objects with a generator expression ((first, second) for first in self.basic_objects for second in self.basic_objects). RED: add raise Exception inside with self.subTest(pair=(first, second)) to verify all one hundred subtests fail. GREEN: remove raise Exception. REFACTOR: remove commented loops and fix indentation. Another way: replace the generator expression with itertools.product(self.basic_objects, self.basic_objects). Terminal shows NameError: name 'itertools' is not defined (Did you forget to import 'itertools'?). Add import itertools to pass. Verify with raise Exception again. Simplify with the repeat parameter: itertools.product(self.basic_objects, repeat=3) triggers ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2, got 3). Fix to repeat=2. Git commit 'test_assertion_error with a generator'.
- [test AssertionError with loops | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AssertionError/AssertionError_w_loops.html): Beginner Python TDD tutorial (Jacob Itegboje, Pumping Python): test AssertionError with loops in the assertion_error project so one test can cover many objects. pytest-watcher shows AssertionError. The first loop in test_assert_keyword fails with assert 2 == 'BOOM!!!', then '11' and 'I am alive', until each expectation is the loop variable. Later loops walk None, False, True, 0, 0.0, an empty string, an empty tuple, list, set, and dict. Unittest cores include unexpectedly identical, unexpectedly None, and None != False. A basic_objects class attribute and a single starred expression replace the repeated tuples. Nested loops make test_assertion_error: ten objects by ten objects is one hundred subtests. self.assertEqual on the unequal pairs fails eighty four of them. assert first is second fails ninety. try and except AssertionError run the opposite check, so the grid stays green. The file still has assert_equal, assert_not_equal, test_assert_keyword, and test_assertion_error_w_none.
- [test AssertionError with None | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AssertionError/AssertionError_w_none.html): Continuation of the assertion_error Python TDD project after unittest and the None chapter. Open the existing project (uv run pytest-watcher . --now --patterns "**/*.py", 7 passed), edit tests/test_assertion_error.py, and add assertIsNone / assertIsNotNone next to bare assert and assertIs / assertIsNot in test_assertion_error_w_none. Deliberately trigger AssertionError with the wrong method first: assertIsNotNone(None) → "unexpectedly None"; assertIsNone(False) → "False is not None"; same pattern for True, 0, 0.0, '', (), [], set(), {}. Then green with assertIsNone(None) and assertIsNotNone for every non-None value (False, True, empty containers, object attributes an_integer/a_float/…). Remove the commented wrong calls; keep the triple form (assert + assertIs* + assertIsNone/assertIsNotNone). Git commit 'use assertIsNotNone and assertIsNone'. Shows how None-specific unittest methods remove repeating None in assertIs(x, None) / assertIsNot(x, None) while still teaching raise-by-negation error strings. Pumping Python by Jacob Itegboje.
- [test AssertionError with unittest | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AssertionError/AssertionError_w_unittest.html): Pumping Python TDD continuation: "test AssertionError with unittest" in the assertion_error project. Move the existing test_* functions into TestAssertionError(unittest.TestCase), add self as the first method argument, and pair each helper/bare assert with unittest methods (assertEqual, assertNotEqual, assertIs, assertIsNot). See the unittest cores this chapter actually quotes: "AssertionError: True != False", "2 == 2", "'11' == '11'", "unexpectedly identical: None", "False is not None", "0 is not 0.0", "0 == 0.0", plus TypeError when a method is defined without self. Then extract repeated locals (an_integer=0, a_float=0.0, a_string, tuple, list, set, dict) into object attributes used as self.an_integer across test_assertion_error_w_none/false/true — no setUp. will_not_run stays skipped until renamed test_will_not_run. uv run pytest-watcher . --now --patterns "**/*.py", git commit after each move, remove the commented lines. Builds on the functions chapter (7 passed at open).
- [assertion_error | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AssertionError/index.html)
- [what is an attribute? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/exceptions/AttributeError/AttributError.html): What causes AttributeError in Python? Step-by-step TDD tutorial in the attribute_error project that deliberately triggers AttributeError: module 'src.attribute_error' has no attribute 'variable_00' (and with "Did you mean" suggestions in later steps). Side-effect NameError: name 'variable_00' is not defined when a bare name is not assigned yet, and TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable when a name assigned None is called as a function. Fix by adding 10 module variables (chained from None) then 10 functions (each returning the previous) in src/attribute_error/__init__.py (uv init already creates that package file; GREEN deletes the stub then defines names). Tests use bare attribute access and calls (no assert statement needed for the main tests; the access itself must not raise). The script adds tests/test_truth_table.py and pytest-watcher. The first test fails with AssertionError True is not false from self.assertFalse(True); change True to False and the test passes. The hub links Nullary Operations (logical_true, logical_false — no inputs), Unary Operations (logical_identity returns the input, logical_negation/NOT returns the opposite with not), all 16 Binary Operations (contradiction, AND/logical_conjunction, OR/logical_disjunction, NAND, NOR, XOR/exclusive_disjunction, material implication, project_first/second, negate_first/second, tautology), the blank-file test truth table tests challenge, and projects. Reuses assertTrue and assertFalse; every truth-table operation in these chapters returns only True or False. Later chapters show AttributeError module has no attribute, TypeError takes N positional arguments, and AssertionError None is not true. Part of Jacob Itegboje Pumping Python TDD series.

Rename tests/test_truth_table.py to test_nullary_unary.py, import src.truth_table, and build Nullary Operations (logical_true always returns True; logical_false always returns False — zero inputs) then Unary Operations (logical_identity returns the_input; logical_negation aka not returns not the_input — one input). Reuses assertTrue and assertFalse; ends with unary truth-table review and test_logical_negation_aka_not. Part of the truth_table project after project setup.

Add a denials dictionary mapping card_expired, above_daily_limit, not_right_pin, and not_enough_cash to their denial messages in test_atm. GREEN: change 'BOOM!!!' to expectation so the test passes. REFACTOR: remove the per-branch self.assertEqual calls so one self.assertEqual(result, expectation) covers all 16 cases; observe the test is slower due to dictionary lookup. Continues the Car project: one ``test_car_ignition`` nests four ``for`` loops over ``(False, True)`` for ``start_is_pressed``, ``key_is_close``, ``brake_is_pressed``, and ``in_park``, and names each case with ``unittest`` ``subTest``. ``uv run pytest-watcher . --now --patterns "**/*.py"`` reports ``SUBFAILED``. ``assertEqual(result, 'BOOM!!!')`` fails all 16 cases: fifteen are ``AssertionError: False != 'BOOM!!!'`` and the all-true case is ``AssertionError: True != 'BOOM!!!'``. ``assertFalse(result)`` leaves one failure, ``AssertionError: True is not false``, when start, key, brake, and park are all true. A ``try`` that catches ``AssertionError`` and then calls ``assertTrue`` makes the loop pass. The other ignition tests are removed because this loop covers them. ## Objects

- [family ties | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/objects/family_ties.html): Step-by-step TDD tutorial on Python cooperative multiple inheritance (family ties chapter), Method Resolution Order (MRO), super() for parent __init__ calls, and inheriting from a Person base class built in prior chapters. Follow red-green-refactor to create Doe, Blow, Smith (class attr eye_color), Jane, Joe, Mary (Joe + Jane), John, Lil (Mary + John) with custom last_name and eye_color. Diagnose and fix real beginner errors shown: TypeError: Blow.__init__() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given, TypeError: got an unexpected keyword argument 'last_name', TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument, AttributeError: module 'src.family_ties' has no attribute 'Blow', AssertionError: 'brown' != '', "is not an instance of", initial AssertionError: True is not false. Uses only local variables in TestFamilyTies methods (no setUp), assertIsInstance/assertNotIsInstance/assertIsSubclass on objects vs instances, dir() comparisons. Builds directly on how_to/make_person (Person + factory), objects, and inheritance ("everything is an object").
- [objects | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/objects/index.html)
- [what is an object? | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/objects/inheritance.html): Step-by-step Python TDD tutorial for beginners on "everything is an object": plain pytest functions (no unittest.TestCase) with bare assert isinstance() and assert issubclass() to prove WPass/WParentheses/WObject (class with pass, (), and (object)), None (instance of object but not a class), bool, int, float, str, tuple, list, set and dict all inherit from object. Instance vs subclass is the () after the name; issubclass(WPass(), object) and issubclass(None, object) raise TypeError: issubclass() arg 1 must be a class. dir(object) lists 24 dunders including __init__ (version caution). Real errors: NameError name 'WPass' is not defined, AssertionError assert not True, TypeError issubclass arg 1 must be a class. Project uv init objects, tests/test_objects.py, pytest-watcher, git. Jacob Itegboje Pumping Python.

Open objects; uv run pytest-watcher . --now --patterns "**/*.py". test_what_is_an_object loops WPass, WParentheses, WObject, bool, int, float, str, tuple, list, set, and dict. Red uses assert not isinstance(an_object(), object) and the terminal shows AssertionError: assert not True (pytest), then assertNotIsInstance shows AssertionError such as False is an instance of <class 'object'>, 0 is an instance of <class 'object'>, and {} is an instance of <class 'object'>. assert not issubclass then assertNotIsSubclass shows AssertionError: <class 'bool'> is a subclass of <class 'object'> (same shape for the other classes). Green switches each line to isinstance, assertIsInstance, issubclass, and assertIsSubclass. Refactor removes the repeated tests and keeps test_is_none_an_object (None is not a class, so issubclass stays commented) and test_dir_object. git commit -am 'extract test_what_is_an_object'. Review: a for loop removes repetition from the tests. What is next: test telephone with loops.

- [objects | pumping python: how I solve problems with Test Driven Development](https://www.pumpingpython.com/objects/objects.html): Step-by-step TDD tutorial for transitioning from dictionary factories to Python objects. Learn the class keyword, __init__ constructor, self parameter, instance attributes, and unittest.TestCase.setUp. Learn how to systematically diagnose and fix common beginner bugs: TypeError: Person() takes no arguments, TypeError: got multiple values for argument 'first_name', NameError: name 'self' is not defined, SyntaxError: parameter without a default follows parameter with a default, and AttributeError: object has no attribute. Master object inspection using the dir() function.
